name: Kerma
place: the Nile above the Third Cataract, in Nubia
desc: The first great kingdom of inner Africa, whose people herded cattle in thousands, made pottery as thin as eggshell, raised huge mud-brick temples called deffufas, and were famed as archers in the 'Land of the Bow'.
source: Excavations at Kerma by George Reisner (1913–16) and Charles Bonnet (from 1977); Egyptian records of Kush

belligerent: hit a running antelope at a hundred paces
gluttonous: brought the whole herd through the dry season without losing a calf
cautious: fired a cup so thin that the light showed through it
devout: climbed the stair of the great deffufa to make the offering at sunrise

inventions.name: Bow of Ta-Seti
inventions.source: Egyptians called Nubia Ta-Seti, 'the Land of the Bow', and hired Nubian archers for their armies
inventions.desc: A long, powerful bow and arrows tipped with flint: +2 attack, hunting is 10% faster.

inventions.name: Eggshell Pottery
inventions.source: Kerma beakers: red pots with a shiny black rim and a silver band between, some barely 2 mm thick
inventions.desc: Tulip-shaped beakers, red below and gleaming black at the lip: +2 mood, the stores hold 10 more.

inventions.name: The Deffufa
inventions.source: The Western Deffufa at Kerma, a solid mud-brick temple still about 18 m high
inventions.desc: A great tower of mud brick with a stair to the roof, where the offerings are made: rites bring 15% more devotion, +1 mood.
inventions.hint: Needs the Tribe & Agrarian Era, and builders who keep the rites.

inventions.name: The Great Herds
inventions.source: Cattle were the wealth of Kerma; some graves were ringed with thousands of cattle skulls
inventions.desc: Herds counted in the thousands, the true wealth of every family: the stores hold 25 more, hunger grows 5% slower.
inventions.hint: Needs Beast Domestication, and long days on the pasture.

foods.name: Sorghum Porridge
foods.source: Sorghum was first cultivated in eastern Sudan, by about 3000 BCE (Butana Group sites)
foods.desc: Ground sorghum stirred into a thick porridge: hunger grows 10% slower.

foods.name: Soured Milk
foods.desc: Milk left to sour in a gourd, the herder's daily food: hunger grows 5% slower, food spoils 5% slower.

finds.name: Wild Sorghum
finds.desc: Tall grass with heavy red seed heads that thrives in the heat. Gathering it brings farming closer.

finds.name: Desert Gold
finds.source: The Eastern Desert of Nubia held the richest gold mines of the ancient world
finds.desc: Veins of gold in the quartz of the desert hills, crushed and washed by hand.

people.name: Hamar
people.desc: He knows the name and the mother of every cow in the herd.
memory: drove off a lion from the cattle with a burning branch

people.name: Nehsi
people.desc: She can string a bow that two men cannot bend.
memory: shot a vulture out of the sky to win her bow

people.name: Nedjeh
people.source: A stela from the fortress of Buhen, c. 1650 BCE, names him as the ruler an Egyptian served
people.desc: One of the few kings of Kerma whose name is known, from an Egyptian who boasted of serving him.

people.name: Awawa
people.source: Egyptian execration texts (c. 1900 BCE), which wrote the names of foreign rulers on pots and smashed them
people.desc: A ruler of Kush feared enough that the Egyptians wrote his name on bowls to break in a curse.

people.name: Sekhi
people.source: The Kamose stela: the Hyksos king Apepi sent a letter to the ruler of Kush proposing an alliance against Thebes; Kamose caught the messenger
people.text: a messenger who slipped past the Egyptian forts by the desert road, carrying a letter from a king in the far north.
memory: crossed the western desert alone by the oases
people.desc: The game's name for the messenger of the Hyksos king, whose real name is not recorded.

people.name: Abkur
people.label: Abkur, Lord of the Bow
people.desc: No archer in the world can match him. Combat 8, Foraging 6.

people.name: Abala
people.label: Abala, Mother of the Thousand Horns
people.desc: Her herds cover the plain. Foraging 7, Trade 5.

people.name: Dakka
people.label: Dakka, Raiser of the Deffufa
people.desc: A builder who raises mountains of mud brick. Crafting 8.

events.title: Raid on the North
events.source: The tomb of Sobeknakht at Elkab describes a great invasion of Upper Egypt by Kush and its allies, c. 1575 BCE
events.text: The northern forts have grown weak. The war leaders want to sweep down the river and bring back the statues and the gold of the north.

options.label: Raid the north

do.remember: raided down the river and came back with the statues of the north

options.result: The raiders return with statues, gold and cattle. Their enemies will not forget.

options.label: Trade instead
options.result: Gold goes north, grain and linen come south.

events.title: The Horns of the Herd
events.source: At Kerma, the skulls of cattle killed at a funeral were laid in rows at the south side of the grave mound
events.text: A great herder has died. The family asks: shall his cattle be feasted and their horned skulls laid in a crescent round his grave, so all can see how rich he was?

options.label: Lay the horns around the grave
options.result: The village feasts for days. A ring of horns gleams white around the grave.

options.label: Keep the herd for the living
options.result: The herd passes to his children, whole.

events.title: The Pastures Burn
events.text: The grass along the river is gone. The herders want to drive the cattle far south, where the rains still fall.

options.label: Drive the herds south
options.result: The young men go south with the herds. They will be back with the rains.

options.label: Cut fodder by the river
options.result: Everyone cuts reeds and leaves for the cattle. It is hard work, but the herd stays.

tales.name: Why We Are the Land of the Bow
tales.source: A story made up around the Egyptian name for Nubia, Ta-Seti
tales.text: Long ago the first hunter of our people prayed to the sun for a weapon that could reach farther than a lion can leap. The sun bent one of its rays into a curve and strung it with a hair from its beard. Since then every child of ours is born with an archer's eye.

tales.name: The Cow Who Carried the Moon
tales.source: A story made up around the cattle cults of the Nile valley
tales.text: Once the moon fell into the river and could not climb out. All the animals tried to lift it, but only a great cow was strong enough. She carried it home on her horns, and the moon was so grateful that it left its shape on every cow's head.

tales.name: The Fire on the Roof
tales.source: A story made up around the Western Deffufa
tales.text: When the great temple was finished, the builders lit a fire on its roof so high that the herders three days away could see it. They followed it home. Ever since, whoever is lost in the desert looks for the deffufa's fire.
tales.moral: a people needs a light to come home to

tales.name: The Feast of the Returning Herds
tales.source: A story made up around the herding year
tales.text: When the rains come and the herds return from the south, every family brings out its best milk and the drums are played all night. The young herders show off the cattle they have raised, and the girls judge whose are fattest.
